summary: The article provides a generally accurate overview of Zerodha's new arbitrage fund and the taxation of arbitrage funds in India, with most claims verified by recent financial news and tax regulations. However, there are some discrepancies regarding the exact LTCG and STCG tax rates and exemption limits, which have seen recent changes.

claims.claim: Zerodha Fund House has launched an arbitrage fund, designed for managing short-term surplus cash.
claims.note: Multiple sources confirm the launch of Zerodha Arbitrage Fund for short-term cash management.

claims.claim: The minimum investment for this New Fund Offer (NFO) starts at ₹5,000.
claims.note: Several sources confirm the minimum investment for Zerodha Arbitrage Fund NFO is ₹5,000.

claims.claim: Arbitrage funds are taxed as equity-oriented mutual funds, which can be advantageous for holding periods over one year.
claims.note: Arbitrage funds maintain at least 65% equity exposure and are taxed as equity-oriented mutual funds.

claims.claim: Short Term Capital Gains (STCG): If you redeem your units within one year of purchase, any gains are considered STCG and are taxed at a flat rate of 15% (plus cess and surcharge, if applicable).
claims.note: As per recent updates (July 23, 2024), STCG on equity-oriented mutual funds is generally taxed at 20% (plus surcharge and cess) if the sale took place on or after this date. Before July 23, 2024, the rate was 15%.

claims.claim: Long Term Capital Gains (LTCG): If you hold your units for more than one year, any gains are treated as LTCG. LTCG from equity-oriented mutual funds are exempt up to ₹1 lakh in a financial year. Gains exceeding ₹1 lakh are taxed at a rate of 10% (plus cess and surcharge, if applicable), without the benefit of indexation.
claims.note: Recent updates (post July 23, 2024) indicate that the LTCG exemption limit for equity-oriented mutual funds has increased to ₹1.25 lakh, and gains exceeding this are taxed at 12.5%. Before this date, the exemption was ₹1 lakh and the tax rate was 10%.

claims.claim: Long-term capital gains from debt funds (held for more than 3 years) are taxed at 20% with indexation benefit.
claims.note: For debt funds purchased on or after April 1, 2023, all gains are taxed at the investor's income tax slab rate, irrespective of the holding period, and without indexation benefit. For investments made before April 1, 2023, and held for more than 36 months, LTCG was taxed at 20% with indexation.

claims.claim: Many arbitrage funds have an exit load, typically 0.25% to 0.50%, if units are redeemed within a very short period, often 7 to 30 days.
claims.note: Several sources confirm that arbitrage funds typically have an exit load, often ranging from 0.25% to 1% for redemptions within a short period (e.g., 7 to 30 days).

article_title: Zerodha's New Arbitrage Fund: Short-Term Cash Management
